connexin_and_fin_length.phenotype_in_papers_words: "In zebrafish, mutations in the gap junction gene connexin43 lead to short bony fin ray segments that give rise to the short fin phenotype. The sof(b123) mutant exhibits fins that are half the length of wild-type fins and have reduced levels of cx43 mRNA." (Hoptak-Solga et al. 2008, Dev Biol 317:541-548, PMID 18406403, doi 10.1016/j.ydbio.2008.02.051). And: "The molecular identification of the fin length mutant short fin (sof), which causes defects in the length of bony fin ray segments ... we demonstrate that the sof phenotype is caused by mutations in the connexin43 (cx43) gene." (Iovine et al. 2005, Dev Biol 278:208-219, PMID 15649473, doi 10.1016/j.ydbio.2004.11.005). Gain of function goes the other way: "the cx43lh10 allele, which has increased Cx43 protein levels, exhibits increased regenerate length and segment length. These phenotypes are rescued by Gap27" (Bhattacharya et al. 2021, Development, PMID 32541014, doi 10.1242/dev.190512). Coupling is the relevant variable: "ionic coupling assays revealed allele-specific differences in coupling efficiency and gating ... measurable differences in Cx43 function may be correlated with the severity of defects in bone length" (Hoptak-Solga et al. 2007, FEBS Lett, PMID 17599838, doi 10.1016/j.febslet.2007.06.030).

connexin_and_fin_length.relation_to_potassium_channel_story: The fetched sources DO connect the two stories experimentally in one place: Seaver et al. 2025 (PMID 40912447, doi 10.1016/j.ydbio.2025.09.001) report that 'the increased segment length in response to Xl-Kcna5 overexpression requires Cx43' and conclude 'potassium channels act together with gap junction channels to influence joint formation, and therefore skeletal patterning, in the zebrafish regenerating fin'. A second, preprint-only source (Aramaki & Kondo 2024, doi 10.1101/2024.03.27.587111) puts a hyperactive kcnk5b and a dominant-negative Cx43 under the same cell-type-specific promoters and finds the keratinocyte manipulations change fin size while the osteoblast manipulations change fin ray segment length. Jiang et al. 2024 (PMID 38527087) place Kcnk5b upstream of shha in the pectoral fin bud and PROPOSE, without testing, that gap junctions explain the uniform intracellular K+ within the bud. What the sources DO NOT connect: (1) the channel in the Seaver epistasis is a Xenopus kcna5 transgene, not zebrafish kcnk5b, kcnh2a or kcnj13, so no fetched paper shows a zebrafish fin-length K+ channel allele interacting genetically with gja1b; (2) nothing links gja5a - the connexin with the flying-fish convergent substitution - to fin length, fin ray length or segment length in any species; (3) no fetched source puts a connexin and a potassium channel in the same cell of the pectoral fin by co-expression or co-localisation. On the flying-fish side, the Daane 2021 claim was verified independently from the fetched Data S1 (mmc2.xlsx): sheet 'G - conv. aa subst.' lists gja5a (ENSORLG00000017925) with substitution G329V ticked for E. viridis, O. micropterus and Exocoetidae and ticked in 'fin screens' - so the thread's gja5a claim is CONFIRMED. But the main text's only connexin statement is about a different gene and the opposite signature: 'the gap junction protein cx43, mutations in which cause short fins in zebrafish, is under constrained sequence evolution along the ancestral branch of flying fishes' (sheet 'J - Exocoeidae phylop' lists cx43 as 'con', phyloP p = 0). gja5a is therefore convergently substituted while cx43 is constrained; they are different genes and the paper makes no functional claim about either in fin length. ZFIN's wild-type expression file has no fin or fin-cell record for gja5a at all (brain, heart, vasculature, somite, skeletal muscle, pharyngeal arches), whereas gja1b is recorded in pectoral fin, pectoral fin cartilage, fin fold pectoral fin bud, mesenchyme and regenerating fin.

interactions.what_is_shown: The return leg: blocking Fgf signalling during ongoing regeneration downregulates epidermal sonic hedgehog as well as blastemal msx genes, and tissue-specific interference shows Wnt/beta-catenin in the non-proliferative distal blastema - not in the epidermis, where the pathway is not active - patterns the overlying epidermis through secondary Fgf and Bmp signals.
interactions.experiment_type: Fgf pathway inhibition during ongoing regeneration with in situ hybridization (Poss); tissue-specific Wnt pathway interference, gene expression profiling, chromatin immunoprecipitation and functional rescue (Wehner)
interactions.stage: "during ongoing fin regeneration" (Poss); regenerating caudal fin blastema and outgrowth (Wehner)

sources.title: Roles for Fgf signaling during zebrafish fin regeneration.
sources.quote: Inhibition of Fgf signaling during ongoing fin regeneration prevents further outgrowth while downregulating the established expression of blastemal msx genes and epidermal sonic hedgehog.

sources.title: Wnt/beta-catenin signaling defines organizing centers that orchestrate growth and differentiation of the regenerating zebrafish caudal fin.
sources.quote: Yet, we find that beta-catenin signaling is neither active in the epidermis nor the majority of the proliferative blastemal cells. Rather, tissue-specific pathway interference indicates that Wnt signaling in the nonproliferative distal blastema is required for cell proliferation in the proximal blastema, and signaling in cells lining the osteoblasts directs osteoblast differentiation.

sources.title: Wnt/beta-catenin signaling defines organizing centers that orchestrate growth and differentiation of the regenerating zebrafish caudal fin.
sources.quote: Gene expression profiling, chromatin immunoprecipitation, and functional rescue experiments suggest that Wnt/beta-catenin signaling acts through Fgf and Bmp signaling to control epidermal patterning, whereas retinoic acid and Hedgehog signals mediate its effects on blastemal cell proliferation.

interactions.notes: Caudal fin, both abstracts only. Ligands and receptors are deliberately EMPTY: Wehner 2014 names the mediating pathways (Fgf, Bmp) but neither the individual blastemal ligand nor the epidermal receptor, and Poss 2000's epidermal shh is a readout of Fgf dependence, not the signal itself. Do not fill in gene symbols here without a new source.

interactions.receiver_label: fin osteoblast (shown in the caudal fin)
interactions.what_is_shown: Wnt/beta-catenin signalling in the blastemal cells that line the osteoblasts directs osteoblast differentiation, and the same organising-centre logic makes the non-proliferative distal blastema drive proliferation in the proximal blastema - all indirect, via secondary signals.
interactions.experiment_type: tissue-specific Wnt pathway interference with differentiation and proliferation readouts; expression profiling; ChIP; functional rescue
interactions.stage: regenerating caudal fin, blastema and outgrowth stages

sources.title: Wnt/beta-catenin signaling defines organizing centers that orchestrate growth and differentiation of the regenerating zebrafish caudal fin.
sources.quote: signaling in cells lining the osteoblasts directs osteoblast differentiation. Thus, Wnt signaling regulates epidermal patterning, blastemal cell proliferation, and osteoblast maturation indirectly via secondary signals.

sources.title: Wnt/beta-catenin signaling defines organizing centers that orchestrate growth and differentiation of the regenerating zebrafish caudal fin.
sources.quote: We propose that Wnt signaling orchestrates fin regeneration by defining organizing centers that instruct cellular behaviors of adjacent tissues.

interactions.notes: Caudal fin, abstract only. No ligand or receptor is named in the abstract and the paper's own conclusion is that the effect is indirect, so the signal fields are deliberately empty.

interactions.receiver_label: apical ectodermal ridge pectoral fin bud
interactions.what_is_shown: Slit ligands made by the immigrating fin mesenchyme act through Robo receptors in the apical ectodermal ridge to make the ridge release sphingosine-1-phosphate; the stomp mutant, a slit3 lesion, blisters the fin and the mesenchyme loses orientation and adhesion.
interactions.experiment_type: positional cloning of the stomp mutant (slit3); pathway epistasis with S1P signalling; cell polarity/orientation and adhesion assays
interactions.stage: growing fin bud / fin fold; no numeric stage given in the abstract

sources.title: Slit-Robo signalling establishes a Sphingosine-1-phosphate gradient to polarise fin mesenchyme
sources.quote: We provide evidence that Slit ligands derived from immigrating mesenchyme act via Robo receptors at the apical ectodermal ridge (AER) to promote release of sphingosine-1-phosphate (S1P).

sources.title: Slit-Robo signalling establishes a Sphingosine-1-phosphate gradient to polarise fin mesenchyme
sources.quote: The zebrafish mutant stomp displays defects in fin morphogenesis including blister formation and associated loss of orientation and adhesion of immigrating fin mesenchyme cells. Positional cloning of stomp identifies a mutation in the gene encoding the axon guidance ligand, Slit3.

interactions.notes: Only the abstract could be fetched (Europe PMC fullTextXML returned HTTP 500; NCBI PMC efetch returned metadata and abstract only), so the individual robo paralogue is NOT resolved - the abstract says 'Robo receptors' and I have left receptors empty rather than guess robo1/robo2/robo3. The abstract says 'fin' and 'fin fold' without naming the pectoral fin, so I used the fin-fold mesenchyme node rather than a pectoral-bud-specific one.

signal.pathway: cell-type-restricted membrane-potential / gap-junction manipulation -> fin size (keratinocyte) vs fin ray segment length (osteoblast)

interactions.what_is_shown: Driving a hyperactive kcnk5b or a dominant-negative Cx43 from keratinocyte promoters mainly changes fin size, while driving the same constructs from osteoblast promoters mainly changes fin ray segment length, so the two outputs are separable by cell type.
interactions.experiment_type: cell-type-specific promoter-driven overexpression of a hyperactive K+ channel and a dominant-negative connexin; optogenetic membrane-potential manipulation
interactions.stage: not stated in the abstract (adult fin)

sources.title: Cell-type-dependent bioelectric regulation of fin size and fin-ray segment length in zebrafish
sources.quote: To manipulate bioelectric signaling, we expressed the hyperactive potassium channel mutant kcnk5b W169L or the dominant-negative connexin mutant Cx43 T154A under a common set of cell-type-specific promoters. Cell-type-specific bioelectric manipulation in keratinocytes primarily affected fin size, whereas manipulation in osteoblasts preferentially altered fin-ray segment length.

interactions.notes: bioRxiv preprint (EPMC id PPR830054), not in PMC; only the abstract was retrievable, so the cell-type promoters, allele details and effect sizes are unverified. The abstract does not claim signal transfer BETWEEN keratinocytes and osteoblasts - it shows cell-autonomous, cell-type-dependent outputs - so this record documents a cell-type division of labour rather than a demonstrated sender->receiver transfer.

interactions.sender_label: apical ectodermal ridge pectoral fin bud
interactions.what_is_shown: AER-expressed Fgf16 is required for cell proliferation in the underlying fin bud mesenchyme, and when the AER fails to switch on fgf24 and fgf8 (pdlim7 knockdown) the mesenchymal Fgf response genes pea3 and erm are mislocalised and mesenchymal fgfr2 is lost, so the bud stops growing.
interactions.experiment_type: morpholino knockdown (fgf16; pdlim7) with in situ hybridization for AER and mesenchymal Fgf targets and receptors

sources.title: Fgf16 is essential for pectoral fin bud formation in zebrafish.
sources.quote: A knockdown of Fgf16 function resulted in no fin bud outgrowth. Fgf16 is required for cell proliferation and differentiation in the mesenchyme and the AER of the fin buds, respectively.

sources.title: Pdlim7 is required for maintenance of the mesenchymal/epidermal Fgf signaling feedback loop during zebrafish pectoral fin development
sources.quote: Along with the lack of fgf24 in the AER, other critical factors including fgf8 are reduced, suggesting signaling problems to the underlying mesenchyme. As a consequence of perturbed AER function in the absence of Pdlim7, pathway components in the fin mesenchyme are misregulated or absent, indicating a breakdown of the Fgf signaling feedback loop, which is ultimately responsible for the loss of fin outgrowth.

sources.title: Pdlim7 is required for maintenance of the mesenchymal/epidermal Fgf signaling feedback loop during zebrafish pectoral fin development
sources.quote: At 36 and 48 hpf, fgfr1 was expressed in wild-type pectoral fins throughout the developing mesenchyme ... After knock-down of Pdlim7, fgfr2 levels were significantly reduced at 36 hpf and expression completely absent from the pectoral fin at 48 hpf

interactions.notes: This is the AER-to-mesenchyme leg of the loop in zebrafish. It is supported for proliferation (fgf16 knockdown) and for the mesenchymal Fgf-target readout, but NOT for the textbook consequence of maintaining mesenchymal fgf10: in pdlim7 morphants AER fgf8/fgf24 were lost while fgf10 persisted in the mesenchyme (see refuted_or_unsupported).

interactions.experiment_type: fgf16 morpholino knockdown with shh in situ hybridization (Nomura); fgf24 mutant with shh in situ hybridization (Fischer)

sources.quote: We also show that fgf24 activity is necessary for the migration of tbx5-expressing cells to the fin bud, and for the activation of shh, but not hand2, expression in the posterior fin bud.

interactions.notes: No Fgf receptor is localised to the ZPA in either source, so 'receptors' is left empty rather than guessed. The fgf24 leg is intra-mesodermal at the stage Fischer studied (fgf24 is in the mesenchyme at 24-28 hpf and only later in the AER), so it is not an AER-to-ZPA arrow at that stage - it is included here only as the second line of evidence that an Fgf is upstream of fin bud shh.

signal.pathway: HGF/Met signalling in migrating muscle progenitor cells that populate the pectoral fin

interactions.what_is_shown: CRISPR/Cas9 mutation of zebrafish met severely reduces the migrating-muscle-progenitor-derived musculature of the paired fins, with fewer fibres in the pectoral abductor, a smaller myoD/myogenin fin bud cluster and disturbed pectoral fin function.
interactions.experiment_type: CRISPR/Cas9 mutant; in situ hybridization for pax3a, myoD, myogenin; pax3a:EGFP live imaging; fin function assay

sources.title: The zebrafish HGF receptor met controls migration of myogenic progenitor cells in appendicular development
sources.quote: In this study we used Crispr/Cas9 to mutate the zebrafish met gene and found that the MMP derived musculature of the paired appendages was severely affected. The mutation resulted in a reduced muscle fibre number, in particular in the pectoral abductor, and in a disturbed pectoral fin function.

interactions.notes: Only the receptor side is zebrafish-resolved: this paper does not show which cell in the fin bud makes the Hgf ligand, and the zebrafish hgfa/hgfb genes are not examined. ZFIN's wild-type expression file has no gja1b record for a myoblast or muscle cell type in the fin.

interactions.receiver_label: apical ectodermal ridge pectoral fin bud
interactions.what_is_shown: A newly identified somite-derived lineage invades the AER of the zebrafish fin and induces the apical fold; ablating those cells blocks apical fold formation, prolongs AER activity and increases the amount of fin bud mesenchyme - i.e. this cell population is the timer that shuts the AER-to-mesenchyme signalling loop off.
interactions.experiment_type: lineage identification and targeted cell ablation of the somite-derived apical-fold-inducing cells
interactions.stage: fin bud / AER-to-apical-fold transition; no numeric stage in the abstract

sources.title: A somitic contribution to the apical ectodermal ridge is essential for fin formation.
sources.quote: Here we show that invasion by cells of a newly identified somite-derived lineage into the AER in zebrafish regulates apical fold induction. Ablation of these cells inhibits apical fold formation, prolongs AER activity and increases the amount of fin bud mesenchyme

interactions.notes: No ligand-receptor pair is identified in the abstract, so all signal fields are empty: this is a cell-invasion / tissue-requirement arrow, not a known paracrine one. Abstract only. The sender node ZFA:0000155 'somite' was read from C:/Temp/genotype/raw/zfa.obo and is outside the pectoral fin subtree, hence node_not_in_subtree. The arrow matters for the viewer because it sets how long the AER-mesenchyme Fgf loop runs.

interactions.what_is_shown: hgfa transcripts fill the zebrafish fin buds before and during migratory muscle precursor immigration, and a CRISPR met null severely reduces the muscle those precursors build, above all the pectoral abductor, with disturbed pectoral fin function.
interactions.experiment_type: CRISPR/Cas9 met mutant with muscle fibre counts and fin function assay (Nord); comparative in situ hybridization for Hgf and Met across species with a summary of the zebrafish hgfa pattern (Okamoto)
interactions.stage: "before MMP migration and after the dorsoventral separation of pectoral fin muscle precursors" (Okamoto); embryonic and juvenile paired fin myogenesis (Nord)

sources.quote: we used Crispr/Cas9 to mutate the zebrafish met gene and found that the MMP derived musculature of the paired appendages was severely affected. The mutation resulted in a reduced muscle fibre number, in particular in the pectoral abductor, and in a disturbed pectoral fin function.

sources.title: Stepwise participation of HGF/MET signaling in the development of migratory muscle precursors during vertebrate evolution
sources.quote: As in the early stages of chicken Hgf expression patterns, zebrafish hgfa transcripts are observed in the entire fin buds before MMP migration and after the dorsoventral separation of pectoral fin muscle precursors

interactions.notes: The ligand side is weaker than the receptor side: Okamoto 2018 states the zebrafish hgfa pattern while citing earlier work rather than showing it, and Nord 2019 does not localise hgfa. Okamoto 2018 also shows the arrow is not pan-gnathostome - in shark, Hgf and Met are 'not expressed at the right time in the right place' for fin muscle precursor migration.

signal.pathway: Cx43 -> beta-catenin -> ccn2a -> evx1 repression -> joint formation; Yap signalling also regulates ccn2a

interactions.what_is_shown: The secreted matricellular factor ccn2a acts downstream of Cx43 and, like Cx43, inhibits joint formation by repressing evx1 in the regenerating fin, with beta-catenin and Yap upstream of ccn2a.
interactions.experiment_type: knockdown/mutant analysis with in situ hybridization for evx1; pharmacological inhibition of beta-catenin and Yap

sources.title: Ccn2a acts downstream of cx43 to influence joint formation during zebrafish fin regeneration.
sources.quote: Connexin43 (Cx43) is known to influence skeletal patterning by inhibiting evx1 expression and thereby regulating the timing of joint formation. Here, we demonstrate that cellular communication network factor 2 (ccn2a) also contributes to this pathway. We find that Ccn2a appears to act downstream of Cx43 and similarly inhibits joint formation by inhibiting evx1 expression.

interactions.notes: Ccn2a is a candidate diffusible relay for the Cx43 signal from medial to lateral cells, but no receptor is identified and the paper does not assign ccn2a expression to a named cell type, so the sender/receiver nodes here are the Cx43 medial/lateral geometry taken from Bhattacharya 2021 rather than a result of this paper.

interactions.receiver_label: apical ectodermal ridge pectoral fin bud
interactions.what_is_shown: Mesenchymal Fgf10a acts on the overlying ectoderm to induce and maintain the AER, where it switches on fgf4, fgf8a, fgf16 and fgf24; knocking down fgf16 (which lies downstream of Fgf10) abolishes fin bud outgrowth, and removing fgfr1a, fgfr1b and fgfr2 together abolishes AER gene expression (fgf24, fgf8a, dlx2a) and the fin itself.
interactions.experiment_type: morpholino knockdown; in situ hybridization; CRISPR null alleles (fgfr1a, fgfr1b, fgfr2) in single/double/triple combination
interactions.stage: "at 24 hpf" ... "at 44 hpf"; "by ~30-36 hpf" (Leerberg); fin bud stage (Nomura)

sources.title: Fgf16 is essential for pectoral fin bud formation in zebrafish.
sources.quote: Fgf16 functions downstream of Fgf10, a mesenchymal factor, signaling to induce the expression of Fgf4 and Fgf8 in the AER.

sources.title: Fibroblast Growth Factor Receptors Function Redundantly During Zebrafish Embryonic Development
sources.quote: whereas fgf24, fgf8a, and dlx2a are all expressed in the AER of wild-type animals at 44 hpf, the number of embryos with reduced or no detectable expression by in situ hybridization is greatly increased in the various mutant combinations

sources.title: Fibroblast Growth Factor Receptors Function Redundantly During Zebrafish Embryonic Development
sources.quote: 100% of fgfr1a-/-;fgfr1b-/-;fgfr2-/- triple mutants fail to form any pectoral fins

sources.title: The zebrafish fgf24 mutant identifies an additional level of Fgf signaling involved in vertebrate forelimb initiation.
sources.quote: We show that the zebrafish fgf24 gene, which belongs to the Fgf8/17/18 subfamily of Fgf ligands, acts downstream of tbx5 to activate fgf10 expression in the lateral plate mesoderm.

interactions.notes: Leerberg 2019 adds that fgfr1a, fgfr1b and fgfr2 are all expressed in the developing fin bud and that 'fgfr1a may be particularly important at the mesenchyme/AER interface'; the receptor assignment is therefore by tissue-level expression plus whole-animal mutant combinations, not by a cell-type-resolved receptor experiment. fgf24 is expressed in the mesenchyme early and only later switches to the AER (see aer-to-mesenchyme-fgf24-switch).
interactions.receiver_node_label: apical ectodermal ridge pectoral fin bud

signal.pathway: Fraser complex extracellular-matrix adhesion across the basal epidermis / pre-osteoblast interface

interactions.what_is_shown: Fras1 and Frem2 accumulate on the basal side of the distal-most basal epidermal cells, and in fras1 mutants the regenerating fin blisters sub-epidermally with a disorganised basal epidermis and disorganised adjacent pre-osteoblasts, with fewer and unbranched rays.
interactions.experiment_type: fras1 mutant analysis; single-cell RNA-seq; in situ hybridization; antibody staining; fin regeneration

sources.title: The Fraser complex interconnects tissue layers to support basal epidermis and osteoblast integrated morphogenesis underlying fin skeletal patterning
sources.quote: Fras1 and Fraser Complex component Frem2 accumulate along the basal side of distal-most basal epidermal cells. ... However, fras1 mutant regenerating fins exhibit extensive sub-epidermal blistering associated with a disorganized basal epidermis and adjacent pre-osteoblasts. We propose Fraser Complex-supported tissue layer adhesion enables robust integrated tissue morphogenesis involving the basal epidermis and osteoblasts.

interactions.notes: bioRxiv preprint, abstract only; no published version found by an EPMC author search (AUTH:'Robbins AE' AND AUTH:'Stankunas K'). The abstract states Shh signalling between the two layers persists in fras1 mutants, so the defect is adhesive rather than a loss of the shha->smo signal.

interactions.what_is_shown: In the juvenile pectoral fin, shha:GFP marks basal epidermal cells sitting just distal to the runx2+ pre-osteoblast pool at the tip of every ray, and blocking Smoothened with BMS-833923 abolishes or severely delays ray branching in all seven fins including the pectoral fins, without blocking outgrowth, bone maturation or proliferation.
interactions.experiment_type: shha:GFP and runx2:mCherry live confocal imaging; Smoothened inhibition with BMS-833923; EdU proliferation assay
interactions.stage: "51 dpf juvenile fish" for imaging; "BMS starting at 21 dpf" scored "at 42 dpf"

sources.title: Basal epidermis collective migration and local Sonic hedgehog signaling promote skeletal branching morphogenesis in zebrafish fins
sources.quote: shha:GFP was expressed at and slightly distal to the runx2:mCherry+ pOb-defined fin boundary in all seven fins, including paired pectoral and pelvic fins (). In all cases, branching rays were tipped with two distinct shha:GFP+ domains

sources.title: Basal epidermis collective migration and local Sonic hedgehog signaling promote skeletal branching morphogenesis in zebrafish fins
sources.quote: However, BMS-treated fish showed no or, at best, severely delayed branching in all fins (n=6 per group). ... the near absence of branchpoints confirms all fins employ a common Shh/Smo signaling-dependent mechanism for ray branching irrespective of their evolutionary divergence

interactions.notes: This is the one epidermis-to-skeleton arrow for which I found evidence IN THE PECTORAL FIN. The cell-resolved receptor side (ptch2:Kaede in pre-osteoblasts) and the live-imaging mechanism were done on the caudal fin - see caudal-basal-epidermis-to-pre-osteoblast-shha - so the pectoral arrow is graded necessity, not mechanism, and the ptch2/smo assignment on the pectoral receiver is carried from the caudal fin. This is ray branching during juvenile fin DEVELOPMENT, a different Shh role from the ZPA arrow in the embryonic bud; the same paper shows Shh/Smo inhibition from 2 dpf does not change the initial ray complement.

interactions.sender_label: pectoral fin / epidermal cell (fgf20a source; localisation carried from the caudal fin)
interactions.what_is_shown: The same Fgf machinery keeps the uninjured adult fin from wasting away: transgenic inhibition of Fgf receptors in uninjured fish atrophies all fin types within two months, losing dermal bone, joints and supporting tissues, and a conditional fgf20a mutation causes rapid progressive loss of fin structures in animals that were never amputated.
interactions.experiment_type: transgenic dominant-negative Fgf receptor induction in uninjured adults; conditional (temperature-sensitive) fgf20a and mps1 mutants; marker expression with cell death and proliferation analysis

sources.title: Fgfs control homeostatic regeneration in adult zebrafish fins.
sources.quote: we found that transgenic inhibition of Fgf receptors in uninjured zebrafish caused severe atrophy of all fin types within 2 months, revealing a requirement for Fgfs to preserve dermal bone, joint structures and supporting tissues.

sources.title: Fgfs control homeostatic regeneration in adult zebrafish fins.
sources.quote: Conditional mutations in the ligand Fgf20a and the kinase Mps1, factors crucial for regeneration of amputated fins, also caused rapid, progressive loss of fin structures in otherwise uninjured animals.

sources.title: Fgf signalling controls diverse aspects of fin regeneration.
sources.quote: we performed comprehensive expression analyses and identified fgf20a and fgf3/10a as major Fgf ligands in the wound epidermis and blastema, respectively.

interactions.notes: Wills 2008 says 'all fin types', which includes the pectoral fin, so the receiver is the pectoral fin organ node; but Wills 2008 does NOT localise the sending tissue - the epidermal location of fgf20a is carried over from Shibata 2016 (regenerating caudal fin), so the sender must be drawn as provisional. The receptor is a whole-animal dominant-negative Fgfr1, i.e. not tissue-resolved. Wills 2008 also reports that fin maintenance 'involved low-level expression of markers of blastema-based regeneration', so adult homeostasis runs the regeneration arrows at low gain rather than a separate program.

interactions.sender_label: zone of polarizing activity pectoral fin bud
interactions.what_is_shown: Posterior fin bud Shh signals into the bud: ptch1 is expressed in the posterior margin of the wild-type pectoral fin bud and expands anteriorly when the Hedgehog antagonist hhip is mutated, giving extra radials; a shhb mutation lowers Hedgehog signalling and loses pectoral fin radials; in shh-null sonic you mutants anteroposterior polarity is only transiently established and the fin bud fails to grow and to make an endoskeleton.
interactions.experiment_type: hhip and shhb mutants with in situ hybridization for ptch1 and skeletal preparations, plus pharmacological Hedgehog repression as rescue (Tanaka); sonic you (shh) mutant phenotype analysis (Neumann)
interactions.stage: "at 48 h post-fertilization (hpf)" and "after 5 days post-fertilization (dpf)" (Tanaka); pectoral fin bud (Neumann)

sources.quote: In WT, ptch1 was expressed in the posterior margin of pectoral fin buds (, black arrowhead). Interestingly, in hhip mutants, ptch1 expression was not only observed in the posterior region but also expanded to the anterior region

sources.title: Anterior-posterior constraint on Hedgehog signaling by hhip in teleost fin elaboration
sources.quote: ptch1 and ptch2 encode Hedgehog signaling receptors that compete with Hhip.

sources.title: Anterior-posterior constraint on Hedgehog signaling by hhip in teleost fin elaboration
sources.quote: shhb mutation induced a decrease in Hedgehog signaling during both early and late development, resulting in a defect in pectoral fin radials

sources.title: Transient establishment of anteroposterior polarity in the zebrafish pectoral fin bud in the absence of sonic hedgehog activity.
sources.quote: We show that Shh is required for the establishment of some aspects of anteroposterior polarity, while other aspects of anteroposterior polarity are established independently of Shh, and only later come to depend on Shh for their maintenance.

interactions.notes: Neumann 1999 is the direct limit on the strong form of the classical ZPA claim: in zebrafish some anteroposterior polarity is set up WITHOUT Shh and only later needs it for maintenance. Tanaka 2024 reports that hhip is expressed in the entire pectoral fin bud at 48 hpf, so the Hedgehog-receiving field is the whole bud and not a narrow anterior strip.

interactions.experiment_type: sonic you (shh) mutant analysis (Neumann); fgf16 morpholino knockdown with in situ hybridization for shh and vice versa (Nomura)

sources.title: Transient establishment of anteroposterior polarity in the zebrafish pectoral fin bud in the absence of sonic hedgehog activity.
sources.quote: Finally, we show that Shh is required for normal development of the apical ectodermal fold, for growth of the fin bud, and for formation of the fin endoskeleton.

sources.title: Fgf16 is essential for pectoral fin bud formation in zebrafish.
sources.quote: Fgf16 in the AER and shh in the ZPA interact to induce and/or maintain each other's expression. These findings have revealed that Fgf16, a newly identified AER factor, plays a crucial role in pectoral fin bud outgrowth by mediating the interactions of AER-mesenchyme and AER-ZPA.

interactions.notes: Both sources were read as abstracts only. Neither abstract localises a Hedgehog receptor in the AER itself, so 'receptors' is left empty; do NOT carry ptch1/ptch2 over from Tanaka 2024 (posterior bud margin) into the AER without a source.

interactions.what_is_shown: Genetically ablating the hoxa13a/hoxd13a-expressing fin fold mesenchyme collapses the pectoral fin fold, disorganises the actinotrichia, lowers fgf10a in the posterior fold mesenchyme and shrinks the shha and ptch2 domains of the posterior endoskeletal disc, and the endoskeletal disc itself is smaller by 7 dpf.
interactions.experiment_type: nitroreductase/metronidazole targeted cell ablation in Tg(m-Inta11-beta-globin:YFP-NTR) with TUNEL, whole-mount in situ hybridization and skeletal staining

sources.title: Effects of fin fold mesenchyme ablation on fin development in zebrafish
sources.quote: Treated larvae show a slight decrease in fgf10a transcripts in the posterior fold mesenchyme of pectoral fins compared to controls ( and ). Despite a decrease in fgf10a expression, no change in fgf8a expression is observed at 72hpf in pectoral fins of treated larvae compared to controls ().

sources.title: Effects of fin fold mesenchyme ablation on fin development in zebrafish
sources.quote: In MTZ-treated Tg(Inta11:NTR) larvae, both shha (ZDB-GENE-980526-166), and its receptor ptch2 (ZDB-GENE-980526-44) display a smaller domain of expression along the proximal-distal axis of the posterior endoskeletal disc at 72hpf, as well as a slight anterior expansion () when compared to control larvae

sources.title: Effects of fin fold mesenchyme ablation on fin development in zebrafish
sources.quote: we show that the ablation of fin fold mesenchymal cells during median and pectoral fin development results in fin fold collapse and actinotrichia defects. In addition, we observed endoskeletal disc reduction in the pectoral fin bud

interactions.notes: The authors themselves call the disc reduction indirect - 'We propose that disc size reductions are a secondary effect of the fin fold mesenchyme ablation' and 'Altered shha expression may be due to lower transcript levels of fgf10a or simply an effect of the disc size reduction itself'. Draw this as a tissue requirement with an Fgf/Hh correlate, not as a demonstrated paracrine step. fgf8a was unchanged, which argues the AER-Fgf8 leg is not the route. The same ablation gave premature calcification of the proximal anterior-most pectoral fin rays at 30 dpf.

interactions.what_is_shown: Intracellular K+ falls in both the mesenchyme and the ectoderm of the growing pectoral fin bud and the two tissues change together; kcnk5b is expressed in the mesenchyme, cells overexpressing kcnk5b lower K+ in their untransfected neighbours, and lowering K+ raises fgf8a, fgf10a, shha, aldh1a2, bmp4 and msx2b and enlarges the bud through IP3R-mediated Ca2+ release and CaMKK.
interactions.experiment_type: FLIM of a FRET K+ sensor (KIRIN1) in vivo; mosaic kcnk5b-mCherry overexpression; heat-shock overexpression of kcnk5b/kcnk10a; CRISPR-Cas9 targeting of rcan2 and kcnk5b with mRNA rescue; in situ hybridization and qRT-PCR; pharmacology (IP3R, CaMKK)
interactions.stage: "from 30 hpf to 56 hpf"; "at 48 hpf, a time point in which the growth of the pectoral fin buds is underway"

sources.title: The scale of zebrafish pectoral fin buds is determined by intercellular K+ levels and consequent Ca2+-mediated signaling via retinoic acid regulation of Rcan2 and Kcnk5b

refuted_or_unsupported.proposed: The ZPA is the source of anteroposterior positional information in the zebrafish pectoral fin bud, as Shh is in the tetrapod limb.

In shh-null sonic you mutants some aspects of anteroposterior polarity are set up WITHOUT Shh and only later depend on it for maintenance, so the zebrafish ZPA is not the sole source of anteroposterior information. Separately, the Shh/ZPA module does not account for ray branching: Braunstein 2021 found Shh/Smo inhibition from 2 dpf left the normal complement of 18 caudal rays, and the caudal fin has no polarised shha at all.

gaps.gap: No fetched zebrafish single-cell study of fin tissue reports a cell-cell communication / ligand-receptor analysis for these cell types. Cudak et al. 2024 (PMID 38318374, iScience) scRNA-seq's FACS-enriched epidermal, osteoblast and blastemal fin regenerate cells, and Robbins et al. 2023 scRNA-seq's the regenerating fin, but neither full text contains CellChat, CellPhoneDB, NicheNet, Omnipath, 'ligand-receptor' or 'cell-cell communication'; the same is true of the 2026 Nature Communications fin/limb regeneration multi-omic paper (PMC12923738). Targeted EPMC searches for zebrafish fin scRNA-seq plus CellChat/CellPhoneDB/ligand-receptor returned no such study.

No ligand-receptor database was fetched, so no database-derived pair is recorded. CellChatDB is human and mouse: 'Applying CellChat to mouse and human skin datasets shows its ability to extract complex signaling patterns' (Jin et al. 2021, Nat Commun, PMID 33597522, doi 10.1038/s41467-021-21246-9). Any pair taken from it for a fin cell type would be orthology-inferred and none was needed, because every pair recorded here has a zebrafish-native source except the CXCL12/CXCR4 record.

The Cell Ontology, as served by Ubergraph, places NO marker gene in any of the six cell types. A SPARQL query over CL:0000062 (osteoblast), CL:0000138 (chondrocyte), CL:0000058 (chondroblast), CL:0000134 (mesenchymal cell), CL:0000362 (epidermal cell) and CL:0000056 (myoblast) for any outgoing property whose label contains 'marker' or 'express' returned HTTP 200 with zero bindings.

Bgee has no cell-type-resolved call for any of these genes. In Danio_rerio_expr_advanced.tsv.gz, shha, smo and ptch2 are 'present, gold quality' in pectoral fin (UBERON:0000151), paired fin bud (UBERON:0002531), mesenchyme pectoral fin (UBERON:0003934) and pectoral fin lepidotrichium (UBERON:4000175), but every call is an UBERON anatomical entity, never a CL cell type. gja1b, gja5a, gja5b, panx1a and gjd4 have NO Bgee call for any fin or cleithrum anatomical entity. The Bgee SPARQL endpoint remains refused (HTTP 403) per the brief, so no cell-type query could be run there.

Nothing establishes an interaction involving chondrocyte (ZFA:0001161+ZFA:0009084, ZFA:0000141+ZFA:0009084) or chondroblast (ZFA:0000257+ZFA:0009027) as sender or receiver. ZFIN records gja1b wild-type expression in pectoral fin cartilage (ZFA:0000257) by in situ at Larval:Protruding-mouth, but that is expression, not an interaction, and the source abstract (Chatterjee et al. 2005, PMID 15895415) does not mention fin or cartilage. No gap-junction, contact or ligand-receptor partner for fin cartilage cells was found.

Nothing establishes any interaction for the cleithrum, including cleithrum / osteoblast (ZFA:0000184+ZFA:0009031). No fetched source mentions a connexin, gap junction or ligand-receptor pair in the cleithrum or pectoral girdle.

No fetched source establishes an interaction for pectoral fin fold / mesenchymal cell (ZFA:0005317+ZFA:0009081) or pectoral fin fold / epidermal cell (ZFA:0005317+ZFA:0009183) specifically; the epidermis-osteoblast records are for the fin ray / basal epidermis, not the fin fold.

Pannexins are untested in the fin. ZFIN lists panx1a^nhi6, panx1b^nhi7, panx2^sa12329 and panx3^sa10093/sa12358 alleles, but phenoGeneCleanData_fish.txt records no fin, fin ray or segment phenotype for any panx gene, and no fetched paper reports one.

Connexins other than gja1b have no fin-length phenotype in the fetched record. ZFIN fin/fin-ray phenotypes exist only for gja1b; gja4 alleles give pigment-stripe phenotypes, gja3 cardiac and eye, and gja5a/gja5b none in the fin. gjd4/Cx46.8 couples trunk slow muscle (PMID 38936363) but was not examined in the fin.

No fetched source shows gap-junction coupling between an osteoblast and an epidermal cell, or between a myoblast and any other fin cell type, in the fin. The Aramaki & Kondo preprint manipulates each cell type separately and does not demonstrate transfer between them.

The dmh35 fin-ray and segment phenotype could only be taken from ZFIN's curated annotation, not from the paper's own words: the publisher blocks PMC full text for Henke et al. 2017/2018 (Genetics, PMID 28835471, PMC5629327; efetch returns 'The publisher of this article does not allow downloading of the full text in XML form') and the abstract does not name gja1b. ZFIN rows (phenoGeneCleanData_fish.txt, ZDB-FISH-180503-22, ZDB-PUB-170825-12): 'gja1b | ZFA:0001554 lepidotrichium | PATO:0002364 shortened', 'gja1b | ZFA:0005633 lepidotrichium segment | PATO:0002364 shortened', 'gja1b | ZFA:0005596 paired fin | PATO:0002364 shortened', 'gja1b | ZFA:0005597 median fin | PATO:0002364 shortened'.

No fetched source measures the PECTORAL fin specifically for the cx43 segment-length phenotype. Iovine 2005, Hoptak-Solga 2007/2008, Sims 2009 and Bhattacharya 2021 all measure caudal fin rays; the only pectoral-fin statement is the ZFIN curated 'paired fin shortened' for gja1b^dmh35/+.

No flying-fish (Exocoetidae) molecular or expression data for any connexin, pannexin or ligand-receptor pair; everything here is zebrafish proxy data, and the Daane 2021 gja5a entry is a comparative-genomic substitution call only, with no functional test in any species.

A ligand-receptor pair for a Wnt arrow in either direction between the zebrafish pectoral fin bud AER (ZFA:0000085) and its mesenchyme (ZFA:0000789 / ZFA:0001000). In tetrapod limbs ectodermal Wnt3/Wnt3a and AER Wnt/beta-catenin sit inside the Fgf8/Fgf10 loop; Leerberg 2019 says this has yet to be established in zebrafish.

A Bmp arrow between the AER and the mesenchyme of the zebrafish pectoral fin bud. bmp2b, bmp4 and bmp16 sit in the ZFIN expression list for ZFA:0000085 and bmp4 for ZFA:0001000, and Jiang 2024 shows bmp4 and its target msx2b respond to K+ in the bud, but I found no zebrafish pectoral-fin source placing a Bmp ligand in one of the two tissues and a Bmp receptor (bmpr1aa, bmpr1ba, acvr1l) in the other with a loss- or gain-of-function test.

A dorsoventral arrow from the bud ectoderm to the mesenchyme. wnt7a->Lmx1b (ectoderm to mesenchyme) and En1 in the ventral ectoderm are standard in tetrapod limbs, and wnt7aa and en1a do appear in the ZFIN AER expression list for ZFA:0000085, but I found no zebrafish pectoral-fin functional source, so no arrow.
Gremlin/Grem1-type Bmp antagonism closing the Shh-Fgf loop. I reached it only in mouse (Michos 2007, and in the kidney at that), not in the zebrafish pectoral fin.

A ray-to-interray or interray-to-ray signalling arrow in the ADULT pectoral fin. The interray tissue appears in the fetched sources only as a place where rcan2 is expressed during regeneration (Jiang 2024) and as part of a bioelectric size pathway (Lanni 2019, title only); I found no source naming a ligand in one compartment and a receptor in the other, in either direction, in any fin let alone the pectoral.

Any pectoral-fin REGENERATION source for the epidermis-to-blastema and blastema-to-epidermis arrows. Every regeneration paper I could reach (Poss 2000, Shibata 2016, Wehner 2014, Armstrong 2017, Laforest 1998) used the caudal fin; those arrows are recorded with caudal-fin or fin-generic nodes and must not be drawn inside the pectoral fin without that caveat.

An arrow to or from the pectoral fin MUSCULATURE (ZFA:0000563) after the myoblasts have arrived. The only musculature arrow I could support is the HGF/MET immigration arrow into the bud; I found no zebrafish source for a signal from differentiated pectoral fin muscle to the skeleton, the tendon attachment or the epidermis, nor for a signal to the muscle from the fin skeleton. The Lbx1/Fgf link ('FGF signalling from within the fin bud controls the Lbx1 phosphorylation state') appears only as a citation inside Nord 2019; I did not reach the primary paper.

A signalling arrow to or from the pectoral fin CARTILAGE (ZFA:0000257) at the chondrocyte level. Hedgehog reaches the endoskeletal disc and sets radial number (Tanaka 2024, Lalonde 2018), but I found no zebrafish source for an Ihh/Pthlh-type chondrocyte-to-perichondrium arrow, nor for a cartilage-to-epidermis or cartilage-to-muscle arrow in the pectoral fin.
The S1P receptor in the fin mesenchyme and the specific robo paralogue in the AER for the Slit-Robo/S1P loop (Mahabaleshwar 2022): the paper is not open access and the abstract names neither.
A ligand-receptor pair for the somite-derived apical-fold-inducing cells acting on the AER (Masselink 2016): the abstract reports cell invasion and ablation, not a paracrine signal.

An arrow involving the pectoral fin fold (ZFA:0005317) or the fin fold of the bud (ZFA:0005316) as the SENDER to the epidermis or to the AER. The fin-fold arrows I found run mesenchyme-to-AER (slit3), AER-to-mesenchyme (S1P) and fin-fold-mesenchyme-to-cartilage (ablation); the fin fold as an epithelial signalling tissue in its own right is unsupported here.
Any flying-fish source at all. Every arrow here is zebrafish (with one shark/mouse/chick comparison) and must be presented as a proxy for the enlarged pectoral fin, never as flying-fish data.
